observation: The run had two clear systemic issues: many nodes used implausibly high validation from stacked/tuned models and the submitted node was one of those flagged nodes despite unflagged alternatives; separately, several first-occurrence execution failures were concrete and repetitive (mixed feature-name types, expensive CV search timing out, and invalid StratifiedKFold arguments).
hypothesis: High confidence. AIDE is over-exploring complex stacking/hyperparameter-search patterns that both inflate self-reported validation and consume budget, and without extra guidance it also misses straightforward fixes to common sklearn errors. Adding prompt guidance to prefer believable held-out CV and a submission profile that is more conservative, plus targeted execution-error notes, should steer it toward simpler valid baselines and faster debugging.
expected_behavior: In the next run, fewer nodes should attempt expensive nested search/stacking, fewer timeout and repeated propagation errors should appear, and debug attempts after the cited exceptions should directly normalize column names, remove or shrink search, or fix StratifiedKFold shuffle/random_state. Submission choice should more often avoid nodes with suspiciously extreme validation when unflagged alternatives exist.
regression_risks: More conservative selection and simpler-model guidance may reduce occasional upside from genuinely strong complex models; lowering tree_topk may narrow exploration diversity. The hook only addresses observed error families and could be irrelevant on unrelated tasks.
summary: I added explicit notes to distrust train-like stacked AUCs, favor simple leak-resistant CV, and prefer believable unflagged candidates for submission. I also added targeted error diagnoses for mixed sklearn feature-name types, search-related timeouts, and the StratifiedKFold shuffle/random_state mistake, and enabled a more conservative submission profile.
